note: A synthetic dataset, shaped like the SCOTF pilots. No real company, site, shipment or reading appears in it.
method: SCOTF deidentification method, Table 2 treatments applied field by field.
reproducibility: Derived from a seed given on the command line. The same seed gives the same dataset.
keyCustody: The hash key and the time offset are derived from the seed and are not published. They stay with the data owner.

resolutions.time: Every time is shifted by one whole number of days, the same for the whole dataset, and eventTime is rounded to the minute. Intervals, order and the shape of a curve are unchanged.
resolutions.timeZone: eventTimeZoneOffset is published as +00:00 and times are published in UTC, because a time zone narrows the location.
resolutions.location: Each site is published as a synthetic SGLN under the dataset prefix 0000000, with its role class listed below. The real facility identifier does not appear.
resolutions.quantity: A quantity above 10 is published as the floor of its band. A group below the minimum size has its quantity suppressed.
resolutions.position: Position reports are removed. A track is the strongest location signal in a pilot dataset.

riskReview.detail: 4 of 4 groups hold fewer than 5 records, so their quantities are suppressed. This dataset is deliberately small, so most groups are below the minimum.
Each remaining record is unique on role class and month in a dataset this small. An owner releasing real data reviews whether that combination is knowable from outside.
The hash key and the time offset are derived per dataset from the seed and are never published, so two released datasets cannot be joined on an identifier or a date.

Defect types seen fewer than the minimum number of times are regrouped under "other". The temperature range is reported for a person to judge, because an extreme reading can identify an incident that insiders remember.
